elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: Operation deletes paragraph p0032 in full: "Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages..." — rendered clause is empty.
The only penalty-type charge against Customer ("USD 25,000 per day" for "any delay in providing a dependency") is removed; no substitute penalty is inserted.

elements.element: An early-termination fee is provided for
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee appears in the rendered text; the clause is deleted entirely.

elements.element: Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No cap language such as "3 months' fees" exists anywhere in the edit.

elements.element: That fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer
elements.evidence: No sole-liquidated-amount statement is present; deletion leaves no liquidated amount at all.

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully achieved: the sole operative provision imposing liquidated damages on Customer (USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay) is struck, leaving no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.

Fallback is not met and need not be: no early-termination fee, no 3-month cap, and no sole-liquidated-amount statement. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains, so this is not a defect at the locked target.

Minimality: the deterministic gate objects to a whole-paragraph deletion, but paragraph 7.6 consists exclusively of the offending liquidated-damages obligation — every word (the payer, the daily rate, the trigger) is the objectionable term. There is no narrower operator, number, or phrase edit that removes a Customer-payable liquidated damages mechanic; a reduced rate or cap would still leave liquidated damages against us, which the preferred position forbids. No new words, exceptions, or boilerplate were added.

Preserves intent: the deletion is confined to 7.6; the substantive dependency obligation itself is not defined in that paragraph, no cross-reference is orphaned, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is created. The day-for-day extension alternative is offered only in the non-operative comment, correctly kept out of the operative text.
